report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2/2 of fanout.py: defines fan_out function with resume logic, temperature guard, budget guard, threading, progress callback, and summary dict. Claims checked against code.
risks: line 281-300 | high | policy and system_override parameters are accepted but never used in this chunk; if caller expects them to influence behavior, they are silently ignored. | Check if they are used in _one_call or elsewhere.

line 312-320 | medium | resume skips tasks with existing parsable result files, but if a file exists and is parseable but contains wrong data (e.g., empty answers list), it is still skipped because the code returns if res.answers is truthy. | Confirm intended behavior: should a file with empty answers be re-run?

line 328-330 | low | Exception handling in _run_task catches all exceptions and appends error string; if an exception has no traceback, format_exception_only may produce empty string. | Verify that error messages are meaningful.
line 345 | medium | on_result callback exceptions are silently ignored; if callback has side effects, failures may go unnoticed. | Consider logging or other error handling.

line 367 | medium | The return dict includes 'paid_calls' which is a count of API calls; the docstring claims it's a count, but the claim about 'budget ledger' is uncheckable. | Ensure consistency with budget module.
todos: Verify that policy and system_override parameters are intended to be unused in fan_out (or ensure they are passed to _one_call).
Clarify resume behavior for files with empty answers list.
Consider adding logging for on_result callback exceptions.
Ensure budget ledger references are consistent across modules.

handoff.purpose: Defines the fan_out function: orchestrates parallel task execution with resume, temperature guard, budget guard, and progress reporting.

symbols.name: fan_out
symbols.note: Main public function; creates output directory, spawns thread pool, calls _one_call per vote, writes result files, and returns summary dict.

symbols.name: policy
symbols.note: Parameter of fan_out; type Any | None, default None. Not used in this chunk.

symbols.name: system_override
symbols.note: Parameter of fan_out; type str | None, default None. Not used in this chunk.

symbols.name: temperature
symbols.note: Parameter of fan_out; float, default 0.0. Used in temperature guard and passed to _one_call.

symbols.name: resume
symbols.note: Parameter of fan_out; bool, default True. Controls skipping tasks with existing result files.

symbols.name: on_result
symbols.note: Parameter of fan_out; optional callback called per completed task.

symbols.name: progress_every
symbols.note: Parameter of fan_out; int, default 25. Controls progress print frequency.

symbols.name: _brief_for
symbols.note: Inner function; returns brief string for a task using render_brief.

symbols.name: _run_task
symbols.note: Inner function; runs a single task: checks resume, loops over votes, calls _one_call, writes result file.

claims.text: Never raises for a failing task: a fan-out of 1,200 in which one task dies must produce 1,199 answers and a named failure, not an exception.
claims.why: All exceptions in _run_task are caught and recorded as errors; the loop continues. The only exception that could propagate is from pool.submit or as_completed, but those are caught in the try block and converted to error results.

claims.text: Transport failures are recorded on the result and the queue continues
claims.why: Exceptions from _one_call are caught and appended to res.errors.

claims.text: resume skips any task whose result file already exists AND parses. A file that exists but does not parse is re-run
claims.why: Code checks dest.is_file(), tries to load and parse; if any exception occurs, it falls through to re-run. If parsing succeeds but res.answers is falsy, it also re-runs (fall-through after if res.answers).

claims.text: asking for votes you cannot get is an error at the door
claims.why: The guard checks any(t.votes>1) and temperature<=0.0 and returns a 'refused' state immediately.

claims.text: At temperature 0.0 the decode is deterministic, so every vote returns the SAME answer
claims.why: This is a claim about model behavior; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: a fan-out whose spend cannot be capped does not run
claims.why: If install_process_guard raises an exception, the function returns a 'refused' state immediately.

claims.text: A refusal that returns a different dict forces every consumer to write two code paths, and the one it will forget is the refusal -- so a caller reading `paid_calls` would crash exactly when the answer it needed was 'zero, nothing was spent'.
claims.where: comment in budget guard exception handler
claims.why: The 'refused' return dict includes all keys that the normal 'ran' dict has (tasks, ok, failed, resumed, paid_calls, out_dir, concurrency, results).

claims.text: PAID CALLS, separate from task count: with votes>1 they differ
claims.why: paid_calls is incremented per vote (counts['calls']), while task count is len(tasks).

claims.text: the budget ledger prices reservations at a deliberate worst-case, so a ledger total is a ceiling and never an invoice
claims.why: Refers to budget ledger behavior not present in this chunk.

observations.what: The parameters policy and system_override are documented and accepted but never used in this function; they are presumably passed to _one_call which is not shown.
The resume logic re-runs if result file exists but res.answers is falsy (empty list). This may be intentional but is not explicitly documented.
Exceptions from on_result callback are silently ignored; this could hide callback failures.
The progress print uses print() directly; may interfere with logging or output redirection.
The function returns a dict with state 'refused' or 'ran'; all keys are consistent between the two states.
